title: A Corner in Wheat
description: D. W. Griffith, 1909: a speculator corners the wheat market while the farmers who grew it and the bakers who need it pay. The first trading film ever made.

title: The Lady and the Stock Exchange
description: A Merrill Lynch comedy that ends where it matters — on the floor of the Exchange, under the big board, in the closing credits.

title: Understanding the Dollar
description: A 1953 classroom film explains what a dollar is worth by putting it on a seesaw — and ends with it falling out of the sky as a giant coin.

title: Pursuit of Profit
description: A grocer works his margins on a whiteboard — fixed costs, variable costs, and the 1% that's actually profit — until the numbers make sense.

title: Story of a City: New York
description: A 1947 walk through the financial district — 30 Broad Street, the Exchange facade, and a street sign for Exchange Place.

title: Skyline New York
description: Manhattan from the air in 1956 — the skyline the trading day happens under.

title: Greed
description: Von Stroheim's silent epic: a lottery win lands on ordinary people, and money does the rest. The feature of the Market History shelf.

title: His Girl Friday
description: Cary Grant and Rosalind Russell trade the fastest dialogue in film history across a newsroom desk.

title: Detour
description: A hitchhiker, a borrowed car, and the worst luck in film noir. Shot in six days; remembered for eighty years.

title: The Little Shop of Horrors
description: Roger Corman's two-day shoot: a florist, a man-eating plant, and a very young Jack Nicholson.

title: Carnival of Souls
description: A church organist walks away from a crash and can't shake the feeling the world has gone quiet around her.

title: The Last Man on Earth
description: Vincent Price, alone after a plague — the first filming of I Am Legend.

title: Night of the Living Dead
pd_basis: Theatrical prints omitted the copyright notice
description: George Romero's original: a farmhouse, one long night, and the dead outside. The film that started it all.

title: Plan 9 from Outer Space
description: Ed Wood's masterpiece of sincerity over budget — flying saucers, hubcaps, and total conviction.
